title: Donut segment labels use the wrong hemisphere after start-angle rotation

complexity.rationale: The root cause and fix direction are confirmed: normalize arc-center angles before all hemisphere-dependent label calculations and add Direct and Advanced regressions.

summary: S2 Donut arcs rotate when `startAngle` changes, but SegmentLabel hemisphere classification uses the unnormalized arc-center angle. Labels can be positioned and aligned on the wrong side of the rotated donut.
symptom: When a Donut uses a nonzero `startAngle`, Direct and Advanced labels do not rotate or reposition consistently with their segments. Some labels move to the wrong hemisphere or use the wrong horizontal alignment.
rootCause: packages/vega-spec-builder-s2/src/donut/donutSpecBuilder.ts:153-166 creates arc-center angles from the supplied `startAngle` through `startAngle + 2 * PI` without normalizing the midpoint. For positive rotations, valid arc-center values can exceed `2 * PI`; negative rotations can produce negative values. packages/vega-spec-builder-s2/src/donut/donutLabelCollisionUtils.ts:66 classifies the raw angle with `arcTheta <= PI ? 'right' : 'left'`. That hemisphere field then drives Direct and Advanced label X positions and text alignment in packages/vega-spec-builder-s2/src/donut/segmentLabelUtils.ts. Periodic sine/cosine positioning remains geometrically valid, but the non-periodic hemisphere comparison does not.

comparison.expected: Normalize each arc-center angle to `[0, 2 * PI)` before hemisphere-dependent positioning so labels remain attached to the same segments and switch alignment only when crossing the visual left/right boundary.
comparison.actual: Raw angles above `2 * PI` or below zero are compared directly with `PI`, causing incorrect hemisphere, X position, and alignment decisions.

edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Every label rotates one quarter-turn with its segment and uses the correct visual hemisphere.
Labels rotate one half-turn and swap hemispheres consistently.
Negative arc-center angles normalize correctly before hemisphere classification.
Equivalent rotations produce identical label positions and alignment.
Each label enters the correct hemisphere group before collision packing is applied.

crossCutting.notes: This is static S2 label geometry. S1 uses a separate legacy polar label path and does not share the S2 collision hemisphere field, so parity is not required.

implementationPlan.change: Normalize the arc-center expression to `[0, 2 * PI)` before assigning the hemisphere field used by collision groups and horizontal label positioning.
Add hemisphere-classification regressions for quarter-turn, half-turn, negative, and greater-than-full-turn arc-center angles.
Verify Direct and Advanced label position/alignment encodings consume the normalized hemisphere field when `startAngle` is nonzero.
implementationPlan.lines: Direct and rich SegmentLabel position tests
